system_overview: This module contains a hierarchical, machine-checked proof of the mutual exclusion property for Lamport's distributed mutual-exclusion algorithm. It proves both type correctness and the main safety property (mutual exclusion) by defining and verifying an inductive invariant. The proof applies to an arbitrary number of processes and arbitrary clock values, not just finite instances. It is designed to be checked by the TLA Proof System (TLAPS).
actors_and_components: The module extends the main algorithm specification and imports sequence theorems and the proof system backend pragmas. It references the same set of processes and communication channels as the base specification.
state_variables: This module does not introduce new state variables. It reasons about the state variables defined in the base algorithm specification: local clocks, request records, acknowledgment sets, message channels, and the set of processes in the critical section.
initial_state: The proof establishes that the initial state satisfies the type correctness invariant and the inductive invariant.
actions: No new actions are defined. The proof reasons about the actions defined in the base specification (requesting, receiving requests, receiving acknowledgments, entering the critical section, exiting, and receiving release messages) to show that each preserves the inductive invariant.
safety_properties: The proof establishes mutual exclusion: at most one process occupies the critical section at any time. It also proves type correctness as an invariant. The proof strategy uses an inductive invariant that implies mutual exclusion and is preserved by every action.
additional_assumptions: The proof depends on the standard proof library modules (sequence theorems, natural number induction, well-founded induction, and function properties). It requires TLAPS for machine verification of the proof obligations.
